rules.why: Kernels before 4.8 stop seccomp before ptrace's syscall-enter; proot's seccomp mode aborts (IS_IN_SYSENTER). Android 9 on 4.4.
Without seccomp acceleration XFCE stayed black on one Android 9 / 4.4 emulator (xfwm4 deadlock); real 4.4 phones have reported working desktops, so this only warns (may stay black).
glibc 2.39+ calls fchmodat2, which proot passes untranslated: the guest path doesn't exist on the host (ENOENT). Void.

Before Linux 5.8 statx has no mount id, and under proot name_to_handle_at isn't there either: systemd 256+'s chase() fails with EUNATCH ('Protocol driver not attached'), so sysusers/tmpfiles can't read their config and sudo, dbus and the desktop stay unconfigured (Kali on a Redmi Note 7 Pro, 4.14; andronix-a9, 4.4). The shim gives statx a mount id per filesystem. Keyed on the kernel, not the probe: on 32-bit arm with old kernels Termux's proot crashes the in-distro probe (Go: 'futexwakeup ... returned -38'), so a probe-keyed rule never fired there (Kali armhf, Galaxy A13 5G, 4.14). The shim changes nothing where the kernel gives the mount id.

Kernels before 3.15 have no open file description locks (fcntl F_OFD_SETLKW: EINVAL). systemd 256+ takes /etc/.pwd.lock that way, so sysusers and systemd's postinst stop with 'Failed to take /etc/passwd lock: Invalid argument' (support #436 Kali, Galaxy S6 edge+ on 3.10.61; #438 Ubuntu KDE, Fire 5 on 3.10.108). The shim turns F_OFD_* into the classic POSIX lock commands. Keyed on the kernel (32-bit arm can't run the in-distro probe).

The same shim wherever the probe sees statx give no mount id, whatever the kernel: ChromeOS ARC on kernel 5.10 reports statx_mnt_id missing (support #326's probe), and mount-id-shim, keyed on kernel < 5.8 (kept for 32-bit arm, where the probe can't run), misses it. The shim fills the id only when the kernel didn't, so it is a no-op elsewhere.

On x86 glibc's creat() is the legacy creat syscall, and Android's x86 app sandbox (ChromeOS ARC on a Chromebook) doesn't allow it: ENOSYS. dnf's key import (librepo) writes every key with creat(), so each Fedora package install failed with 'Failed to create file ... Function not implemented' (support #326, Chromebook grunt, x86_64). The shim makes creat() an open() with O_CREAT|O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC. Other CPUs have no creat syscall (the probe answers ok).

On some old kernels proot answers fchmodat2 with a wrong errno (ENETDOWN on andronix-a9, 4.4) instead of ENOSYS, so glibc 2.39+ doesn't fall back and every chmod of a symlink fails ('Cannot change mode: Network is down'). The fchmodat shim never calls fchmodat2.
Android 12+ kills background processes past 32 (phantom process killer): long installs and desktops die with signal 9.
